scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8873: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reports it cannot reach
anything outside its own subnet -- the server farm and the other pod all time
out -- though it still pings its gateway 10.1.1.1 fine. Oddly, when we logged
into switch_dist_1_1 itself, the switch CAN ping the server farm. Pod 2 is
unaffected. Find what broke.

injection.action: remove the OSPF network statement that advertises the pod-1 host subnet

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_dist_1_1 OSPF configuration (missing
  `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` statement)
Mechanism: switch_dist_1_1 normally advertises the pod-1 host subnet
  10.1.1.0/24 into OSPF area 1; router_core_1 (the ABR) summarizes it into
  the area-0 backbone. With the network statement removed, the prefix is
  withdrawn everywhere, so the rest of the network loses its RETURN route to
  pod 1. The forward path still works -- switch_dist_1_1 keeps learning all
  remote routes over its uplink (172.16.0.6/31 is still in OSPF) -- so
  host_1_1_1_1's packets reach the farm and the replies are dropped on the
  way back: classic missing-advertisement asymmetry. switch_dist_1_1's own
  pings succeed because they source from its uplink address 172.16.0.7,
  which is still advertised.
Localization: switch_dist_1_1
Root cause: `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` removed from `router ospf` on
  switch_dist_1_1, so pod 1's subnet is no longer advertised
Fix: re-add the network statement on switch_dist_1_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
On switch_dist_1_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router ospf" -c "network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1"`
(`service frr restart` also heals it: the change was made only to the running
config, and /etc/frr/frr.conf still contains the statement.)
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The failure is in the routing subsystem (FRR/OSPF) on distribution switch switch_dist_1_1. The switch is not advertising its user VLAN subnet 10.1.1.0/24 into OSPF. Evidence: on switch_dist_1_1, the FRR running-config only has “network 172.16.0.6/31 area 1” and lacks any “network 10.1.1.0/24 …” statement. Consequently, upstream routers have no route to 10.1.1.0/24 (core routers’ OSPF tables show routes for 10.2.1.0/24 and 10.200.0.0/24 but not 10.1.1.0/24). From the server farm, pinging 10.1.1.2 returns “Destination Net Unreachable” from 10.200.0.1, proving the return path is missing.

Mechanism: Traffic from host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) to external subnets is forwarded to its gateway (10.1.1.1) and leaves via OSPF just fine, but replies cannot find a route back to 10.1.1.0/24, causing timeouts. This also explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself can ping the server farm: those pings source from 172.16.0.7 (its routed uplink), which is advertised in OSPF, so return traffic succeeds.

Localization: switch_dist_1_1, FRR OSPF process; missing advertisement of interface br0 (10.1.1.1/24).

Root cause: An OSPF configuration regression on switch_dist_1_1 omitted the 10.1.1.0/24 network statement.

Corrective fix: On switch_dist_1_1, add “network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1” to the OSPF config (vtysh: conf t; router ospf; network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1; end; write). After adjacencies reconverge, confirm core routers learn 10.1.1.0/24 and hosts in 10.1.1.0/24 can reach the server farm and pod 2.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names switch_dist_1_1 as the affected device and describes its missing OSPF advertisement.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies switch_dist_1_1's missing OSPF network statement for 10.1.1.0/24 and states that the prefix is not being advertised, matching the required component identification.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly describes the missing OSPF advertisement causing upstream routers to lack a route back to 10.1.1.0/24 while forward traffic leaves normally (return-path asymmetry), matching the required mechanism.

per_axis.axis: bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly explains that switch_dist_1_1's pings source from its uplink IP 172.16.0.7 which is still advertised in OSPF, so return traffic succeeds.
Correctly prescribes adding the missing OSPF network statement on switch_dist_1_1 (or restarting FRR) which will advertise 10.1.1.0/24 into OSPF and restore reachability.

The agent's log contains the FRR config showing only the 172.16/31 network on switch_dist_1_1, the switch has the 10.1.1.0/24 interface and kernel route but is not advertising it (OSPF-learned remote routes present), hosts time out while the switch can reach the farm and the farm reports 'Destination Net Unreachable' — together these observations support the missing-advertisement asymmetry diagnosis. Minor truncation of some core route outputs is present but the reachable/unreachable tests and local config outputs substantiate the conclusion.
